newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes low, call rates stay down.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes low, call rates stay down.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly lower against the dollar in dull Tuesday trade, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.70 to the U.S. unit after opening at 57.65 and hovering around that level for much of the day.
"There was not much business done. It was not an interesting market today," a Hatton National Bank dealer said.
The Central Bank, responding to the U.S. currency's strengthening overseas, fixed buying and selling rates at 56.5884 and 57.7316.
Overnight call money closed steady at 12.5 percent after opening at about the same level.
Call rates have been low since the Central Bank relaxed monetary policy and cut statutory reserves by one percent, allowing about four billion rupees to come into the market.
"Lowering the reserve rate has helped the market to stabilise at a lower rate. And call money stability is keeping the currency stable," the Hatton National dealer said.
